gloss: to have influence; to have connections

definitions.gloss: to have influence; to be well connected in a particular place
definitions.explanation: To be known and trusted somewhere well enough that one's word gets things done — a table found at a full restaurant, a favor granted. Literally 'one's face works.' The place or circle is marked with で.

examples.japanese: {父|ちち}はこの{町|まち}で{顔|かお}が{利|き}く。
examples.english: My father has connections in this town.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{業界|ぎょうかい}で{顔|かお}が{利|き}くから{相談|そうだん}してみよう。
examples.english: He has pull in the industry, so let's ask him about it.

examples.japanese: {顔|かお}が{利|き}く{知|し}り{合|あ}いのおかげで、{満席|まんせき}の{店|みせ}に{入|はい}れた。
examples.english: Thanks to a well-connected acquaintance, we got into a restaurant that was fully booked.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}{地元|じもと}で{商売|しょうばい}をしてきたので、{市場|いちば}では{今|いま}でも{顔|かお}が{利|き}く。
examples.english: Having run a business locally for many years, he still has pull at the market.

notes:
STRUCTURE: {顔|かお} (face, reputation) + が + {利|き}く (to be effective).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- 〜で{顔|かお}が{利|き}く: to have pull in ~ (a town, an industry, a company)
- {顔|かお}が{利|き}く{人|ひと}: someone with connections

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {顔|かお}が{広|ひろ}い: to know a lot of people — breadth of acquaintance; {顔|かお}が{利|き}く adds the power to get results
- コネがある: to have connections — plainer and slightly negative, suggesting unfair advantage

USAGE:
Normally admiring, but depending on context it can hint that the person gets special treatment others don't.
